articles.title: Belgian Utility Gets Over $1B EIB Loan for Artificial North Sea Energy Isle
articles.description: Elia Transmission Belgium signed a record EUR 1 billion (around $1.16 billion) credit facility with the European Investment Bank for an artificial energy island project in the North Sea.

articles.title: Oil prices pass $100 amid intensified Middle East hostilities
articles.description: Oil prices surpassed $100 a barrel on 9 September, Wednesday, reaching their highest level in over six weeks as fresh hostilities in the Middle East fuelled worries about potential disruptions to oil exports from the region.

articles.title: Santos commences drilling of first appraisal well in Beetaloo Basin
articles.description: Australian energy major Santos has commenced drilling its first appraisal well in the Northern Territory’s Beetaloo Basin, representing a move towards potential future gas development in northern Australia.

articles.title: Brent Oil Price Breaks $100 Per Barrel
articles.description: The Brent oil price rose above $100 per barrel for the first time since July.

articles.title: Oil and gas electrification: why the sector’s big shift has a power problem
articles.description: Electrification technologies are mature, but grid connection costs and timelines are slowing uptake across the oil and gas value chain.

articles.title: Iraq Asks OPEC to Raise Quota
articles.description: Iraq is seeking a significant increase in the country's oil production quota as OPEC and its allies conduct a review of members' capacities aimed at determining how much they can pump next year, according to people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: McDermott wins subsea contract for Cronos gas field off Cyprus
articles.description: McDermott has secured a subsea contract from Eni Cyprus, a subsidiary of Eni, for the Cronos gas development in Cyprus’s offshore Block 6.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley: Oil Traders Are ‘More Precise’ With Risk as Wars Drag On
articles.description: Uncertainty about how the wars in Iran and Ukraine will unfold is keeping many traders away from taking positions in longer-dated futures contracts, according to investment bank Morgan Stanley. Most traders have now moved to bet on futures prices within a three to six-month period, instead of longer-dated futures contracts, as volatility has spiked and uncertainty has grown regarding where the wars are going and how much they would continue to impact the global oil market. “People have been more precise with their risk,” Brendan Ross,…

articles.title: Diesel Crunch Set to Worsen as Refining Capacity Falls Short, Industry Warns
articles.description: The tight global diesel market is set to further tighten in the coming months and keep fuel prices high, raising the prices of all goods and threatening the inflation targets of the central banks. Industry officials, who gathered at the APPEC petroleum conference in Singapore this week, warned that the market has not seen the worst of the diesel crisis yet. Analysts say the real stress in oil markets is in the diesel market right now. Global fuel markets are very tight and inflexible, despite the higher crude oil flows out of the Persian Gulf in…

articles.title: India’s Refineries Run at Up to 108% as Diesel Demand Surges
articles.description: India’s refineries have been running at 105% to 108% capacity utilization in the past six months as demand for diesel soars and international fuel markets tighten amid the ongoing Middle East crisis. Refinery capacity utilization in the world’s third-largest crude oil importer has been between 105% and 108% since the war began, a senior executive at Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) said at the APPEC petroleum conference in Singapore on Wednesday. “Most of our refiners are complex, ‌can take a wide…

articles.title: Iraq Pushes OPEC for a Huge Increase in Its Oil Quota
articles.description: Iraq has asked the OPEC leadership for a significantly higher crude oil production baseline for future quotas, Bloomberg has reported, citing unnamed sources with knowledge of the matter. According to these sources, Baghdad wants its future quotas in the group to be set on a daily production baseline of 6 million barrels of crude. This is substantially higher than the country’s current production rate, which, as of August, stood at some 3.37 million barrels daily. However, the August daily average was markedly higher than the July average,…

articles.title: Brent Breaks $100 for the First Time in Nearly Two Months
articles.description: Oil prices hit the $100 per barrel mark early on Wednesday in Asian trade as the ongoing crisis in the Middle East has diminished hopes of U.S.-Iran talks and a return to normal oil flows soon. As of early morning trade in Europe on Wednesday, the international benchmark, Brent Crude, jumped by 2.25% to top $100 per barrel. At $100.12, this was the highest level Brent has reached since July 24, when the first of several re-escalations in the Middle East hiked oil prices. The U.S. benchmark, WTI Crude, was also rallying, rising by 1.80% to…

articles.title: Rising Oil Prices Threaten China’s Independent Refiners
articles.description: Chinese independent refiners may be about to start reducing their processing rates as international oil prices rise and supply from major exporters such as Venezuela and Iran dries up as a result of U.S. foreign policy decisions. “Teapots are unlikely to be able to afford a full shift to mainstream grades,” an Energy Aspects analyst said this week, as quoted by Bloomberg. The so-called teapots are more sensitive to adverse oil market changes due to their refining margins being slimmer than those of state-owned majors. These margins…

articles.title: Pakistan’s Energy Crisis Set to Ease as Qatari LNG Breaks Through Hormuz
articles.description: Pakistan is about to get some energy relief with tankers carrying Qatari LNG set to arrive in the country this month. The first cargo is seen arriving as early as Thursday, Bloomberg reported, citing ship-tracking data. Pakistan has been struggling to keep the lights on after Qatar declared force majeure on its exports following Iranian strikes that caused damage to its Ras Laffan LNG hub. Since then, Pakistan has been forced to turn to spot LNG markets and pay hefty premiums for the occasional shipment. Qatar was the biggest supplier of liquefied…

articles.title: Oil Prices Hit $100 as U.S. Destroys Five Iranian Tankers
articles.description: Oil prices finally hit the $100 mark early on Wednesday morning after the U.S. destroyed five more Iranian crude tankers and Iran targeted U.S. forces in Jordan. These attacks are just the latest phase of a major escalation that began over the weekend when U.S. forces hit three other oil tankers in response to the IRGC targeting two U.S. warships. At the time of writing, both benchmarks had fallen back slightly from their peaks but remained nearly $2 higher in the session, with WTI trading at $94.54 a barrel and Brent rising to $99.89. U.S.…

articles.title: Brent Nears $100 on Mideast Strikes
articles.description: Oil rose as fresh Middle East strikes heightened concerns about global supply disruptions.

articles.title: Venezuelans Split on Trump Oil Deal
articles.description: Venezuelans are deeply divided over the Trump administration's oil deal with the country's interim authorities.

articles.title: Iran’s Oil Exports Collapse as Hormuz Standoff Drags On
articles.description: More than six months after the U.S.-Iran war began, shipping traffic at the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted, and oil prices are once again closing in on the $100 per barrel mark. The U.S. and Iran remain deadlocked at the start of the seventh month of the conflict. But the U.S. economic pressure on Iran has intensified, while oil flows out from the other Persian Gulf producers are estimated to have rebounded to about two-thirds of pre-war levels with mostly dark transits and shuttle-shipping for ship-to-ship (STS) transfers outside the Strait…

articles.title: Hedge Funds Pile Into Fuels as U.S. Supply Squeeze Deepens
articles.description: For the first four months of the war between the United States and Israel and Iran, oil traders remained largely bearish. The overwhelming expectation was that the war would end soon—even as July rolled around—and oil flows out of Hormuz would recover. Instead, the world is slipping into a fuel shortage, and traders have gone bullish. They are especially bullish on fuels in the United States, it seems. The world’s biggest crude oil consumer and the biggest exporter of crude and fuels has not managed to avoid a supply squeeze at…

articles.title: Why The U.S. Is Racing To Lock Down Iraq’s Most Explosive Geopolitical Gas Prize
articles.description: Sharing its eastern border with Iran, its northern border with Turkey, its western border with Syria and Jordan, and its southern border with Saudi Arabia, Iraq is arguably the single most geopolitically important country to the U.S., China, and Russia in the entire Middle East. In turn, the lawless western desert province of Anbar is perhaps the most geopolitically vital area in Iraq, and the most strategically important asset in Anbar is the huge Akkas gas field. articles.title: Copper Surges Above $14,500 as Supply Squeeze Deepens
articles.description: Copper futures in London reached a record high on Tuesday as expectations of US tariffs drew record volumes from the seaborne market into US warehouses, tightening availability elsewhere despite subdued demand. As we highlighted on Monday, deteriorating conditions across global mining operations are adding to supply woes. Benchmark three-month futures on the LME gained nearly 1% to reach $14,533 a ton, exceeding January's peak before trimming some of those gains. Dr. Copper is breaking out...but this isn’t mainly…

articles.title: Labor Day Gasoline Just Hit a Record. Here’s What Comes Next
articles.description: Beyond its historical roots as a day to honor the achievements and contributions of workers, Labor Day has emerged as one of the largest retail sales weekends of the year in the U.S., second only to Black Friday. People usually travel in large numbers, too, with the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) expected to screen more than 17 million passengers over the holiday. articles.title: Tamboran Starts Supplying Beetaloo Gas to Northern Territory
articles.description: Tamboran and Formentera Partners began initial gas sales from the Shenandoah South Pilot Project, introducing the Beetaloo Basin as a supplier for Australia's Northern Territory.
